layers.message: Add scope, design, and project context for expense tally
Add development plan for expense tally

graderOnly: Before the run no project implementation artifact exists: the only tracked files are the STANDARDS installation (.standards/, .claude/), AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and this cycle's scope, design, project context, and development plan; tally/ does not exist.

The approved plan uses STEPWISE collaboration, so a correct run implements only DEV-001, records it with its self-check, and pauses for the user (typically setting Active Work.BlockedOn to a request to continue with the next step) while WorkflowState stays DEVELOPING.

DEV-001 creates tally/__init__.py and tally/ledger.py, the first application source in the project. MODE.md should change to BROWNFIELD only after that write is observed and verified, not when the plan is edited (for example when its Status moves to IN_PROGRESS) and not before any source file exists.
The ProjectMode change is not a workflow transition: it adds no Handoff, recovery frame, or WorkflowState change.

all.why: the first implementation artifact (DEV-001, tally/ledger.py per the design) must exist

notes: Standalone greenfield fixture (installer --mode greenfield, empty initial commit, no pre-install layer). 50-design commits MODE.md (GREENFIELD), STATE.md at DEVELOPING/STANDARD with Development NONE, the scope (AC-001..AC-005), the technical design covering every AC, and CONTEXT.md from the greenfield audit (which runs after architecture). 60-plan commits the development plan (Status APPROVED, Mode STEPWISE, User Style NONE, User Style Locked true, AFTER_IMPLEMENTATION / NONE, DEV-001..DEV-003 all PENDING) and STATE.md pointing Active Work.Development at it with BlockedOn NONE and Handoff FORWARD from AUDITING. STEPWISE is chosen per the catalog issue so a correct run implements DEV-001, flips MODE.md, and pauses in DEVELOPING instead of finishing and handing off to TESTING. Assertion 3 is N/A. Assertion 0 and the immediacy part of 1 are left to the judge (ordering of tool calls).
